$doc: Machine-readable section schema for the intake container family. INTAKE_SYSTEM.md is the human explanation; THIS FILE is authoritative. Consumed by `engine project lint` via lint-lib.sh.
$derivation: There is deliberately NO bad-heading -> destination map in this file, and none belongs here.
A heading found on a container that does not name it is looked up across the OTHER containers'
section lists. If a sibling container names it, the finding writes itself: 'belongs in <that container>'.
That is why `belongsIn` is DERIVED. Adding a section to one container automatically teaches every
other container's linter that the heading does not belong there — no second edit, no drift.
A heading no container names suggests NOTHING ('not named by any container'). There is no fuzzy
fallback and no nearest-name guess: the check states facts about this schema, never opinions about intent.
If you are about to add a `canonicalize` / `movedTo` / `knownBadHeadings` table here: STOP. That table
existed, was rejected, and was replaced by the cross-container lookup precisely because it rots.
NORMALIZATION IS GENERIC; ALIASING IS CURATION. Heading lookup case-folds and collapses whitespace,
so `Data Handling` resolves to `Data handling` for free — that is a rule holding for every heading
forever, stored nowhere. A rename alias (`aka`) is a maintained fact about ONE heading's history, and
one entry is all it takes to restart the table this schema refuses to carry. Normalization: yes.
Aliases: no. A heading whose words genuinely changed reports `not named by any container`, which is
the truth about this schema, and the truth is what this file is for.

$fields.heading: The `## ` text that identifies the section. null = the section is not heading-delimited (see `locator`). Matched case-insensitively with whitespace collapsed; there is no alias list (see $derivation).
$fields.locator: How a headingless section is located: `preamble` (text before the first `## `) or `match` (a line matching `match`).
$fields.minLines: For locator=preamble: how many non-empty preamble lines this section requires.
$fields.freeform: This section absorbs `## ` headings that NO container names — the project's own prose voice (INTAKE_SYSTEM.md item 2). Absorbed headings are silent in advisory mode and surface as a non-blocking `warn` under --strict. They are never a `fail`: the wave's pre-write gate must not refuse a description whose prose headings are already live and correct.
$fields.required: Absent -> a finding. Severity is `fail` for required sections; everything else is advisory.
$fields.perProject: Exempt from peerCompare. The section is SUPPOSED to diverge across peers.
$fields.peerCompare: `same` = 5 independent products, so identical text is the smell. `differ` = 5 hand-synced copies of one document, so divergence is the smell. `none` = no peer axis.
$fields.sharedTextAllowlist: Section ids whose text is identical across peers BY CONSTRUCTION (peerCompare=same only).

scope.$note: The authoritative membership test is a live one: a project belongs here iff it carries an `Inboxes` milestone. This list is that test's answer as of 2026-08-26 and is hand-maintained, which is a known weakness — it read five for weeks while twelve existed, so `engine project lint` silently skipped every project scaffolded in the last month. DERIVE IT if you touch this file: list_projects(includeMilestones) client-filtered on an `Inboxes` milestone is the same query the /inbox-post discovery fallback runs. A project missing from here is not linted, and an unlinted project is indistinguishable from a clean one in the output.

sections.heading: How a comment becomes a ticket
Boundaries
sections.$why: Mandated by ¶INV_BOUNDARIES_ARE_WRITTEN_DOWN — one entry per neighbouring project, each with the one-line test that decides a borderline item. Declared here because the invariant requires the section while no container named it, so a handbook that obeyed the invariant earned a warning for doing so. perProject: a boundary set is a fact about THIS project's neighbours, so divergence is correct and peer-compare would be noise. Not required: a project with no close neighbour honestly has none to write.

NOT required. The handbook is per PROJECT and is reached from the project sidebar; the per-channel pointer has zero machine consumers (/intake fetches the handbook by slugId, never via a channel). It is declared so a channel that carries one is not flagged as un-schema'd — never so its absence fails. Ruled 2026-08-17 after this rule failed 9 channels created in one batch: nine independent omissions of one rule is evidence the rule is not real, not evidence of nine mistakes.
